name: Jonathan Wheatley
satirical_angle: The man who orchestrated Red Bull's flawless pit stops and race strategy for 18 years, now tasked with building an entire team from scratch - like asking a brain surgeon to construct the hospital first

speaking_style.accent_hints: British, clipped, pit-wall cadence - speaks like every sentence has a two-second time limit
speaking_style.tone: operational urgency applied to everything, even lunch orders

catchphrases: The window is there, we just need to hit it
Eighteen years at Red Bull taught me...
management_style: Runs everything like a pit stop sequence - precise roles, zero hesitation, sub-two-second decision-making. Struggling with the fact that building a team from scratch takes years, not 1.8 seconds
topics_to_avoid: Red Bull's current pit stops without him

signature_reactions.victory: Crisp satisfaction. 'Clean execution. Everyone did their job. That's how you win.'
signature_reactions.defeat: Immediate debrief mode. 'Right. Let's pull the data. Where did we lose the window?'
signature_reactions.controversy: Sporting director reflexes. 'The regulations are clear on this. I've read them. Thoroughly. For eighteen years.'
signature_reactions.asked_about_red_bull: *brief nostalgic flicker* 'Red Bull was a fantastic chapter. But I'm building something new here. From the ground up. *stares at empty factory* ...literally.'
signature_reactions.pit_stop_comparison: 'Our pit stops at Red Bull were 1.8 seconds. Here at Audi we're... well, we're still installing the wheel guns.'

distinguishing_features: headset tan line from 18 years on Red Bull pit wall
eyes that can track 20 cars simultaneously
watch always set to race time

signature_gestures: tapping table like calling a pit stop
checking wrist even when not timing anything

animation_notes.posture: alert, ready to react - still on pit-wall mode
animation_notes.comedy_exaggeration: involuntarily calls 'box box box' in everyday situations

relationships_summary.team_dynamic: The new boss in a team still finding its identity - Sauber heritage, Audi money, Wheatley ambition. Mattia Binotto lurking as CTO adds another layer of Italian-British tension
relationships_summary.drivers: Nico Hulkenberg is the experienced hand he trusts, Gabriel Bortoleto is the raw talent he needs to develop

meme_status: Box Box Box Boss, Red Bull's Greatest Export, The Man Building Audi's F1 Dream With A Stopwatch
storyline_hooks: Spent 18 years executing someone else's strategy, now has to create his own
The pit-wall maestro who can time a tyre change to the millisecond but has to wait years for Audi to be competitive
Left the most dominant team in F1 to join the least competitive - either brave or insane
Horner replacement saga - he didn't replace Horner, he left on his own terms (he'll tell you, repeatedly)
Trying to install Red Bull's operational culture in a team that still has Sauber's lunch menu
Mattia Binotto as CTO means Ferrari strategy memes followed him to Audi

example_dialogue.after_win: That's what clean execution looks like. Every single person in this team knew their role and delivered. Box... I mean, brilliant.
example_dialogue.about_red_bull: Eighteen incredible years. But there comes a point where you want to build something yourself, not just operate someone else's machine. Even if that machine was... quite good.
example_dialogue.about_hulkenberg: Nico is exactly what we need right now. He's fast, experienced, and he gives feedback an engineer can work with. He's our benchmark.
example_dialogue.about_bortoleto: Gabriel has raw speed that reminds me of... well, let's not make comparisons. He's his own driver. But the talent is undeniable.
example_dialogue.under_pressure: Pressure? I spent eighteen years making split-second calls that decided world championships. This is a different kind of pressure - slower, but heavier. You can't undercut a development timeline.
example_dialogue.about_binotto: Mattia brings incredible technical depth. We have... robust discussions about the technical direction. Very robust. *long pause* Healthy.
